data.title: New Poll: Voters Are Realizing This Income Tax Is Coming for Everyone
data.description:
New Poll: Voters Are Realizing This Income Tax Is Coming for Everyone

New Poll: Voters Are Realizing This Income Tax Is Coming for Everyone

PR Newswire

SEATTLE, Oct. 23, 2026

SEATTLE, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Recent real-time tracking poll shows Initiative 645 is very much in the fight. As voters learn that this really is an income tax coming for everyone, support for repeal rises to two-thirds. The results are consistent with several polls conducted earlier this year, both showing around 67% of voters oppose a state income tax. This latest survey, conducted by NMR Research with voters in Washington's 8th and 5th Congressional Districts, tested the official ballot language against a plain description of the tax. Districts like these, which provide a diverse cross-section of Washington voters, are where statewide majorities are won or lost.

"You can't cut money you don't have, and not a dime of this tax is collected until 2029. The ballot lets that lie stand, but voters know it's not true," said Jaime Herrera Beutler, spokesperson for Vote Yes Repeal the Income Tax. "These numbers show Washingtonians aren't fooled. They know this is an income tax designed to be expanded to working and fixed income families, and that it will capture every person, pension, and nonprofit in the state."

The Results

The survey of 188 voters in Congressional District 8 and 222 in District 5 was fielded Oct. 18-19 and has a margin of error of ±9.5 ±7 respectively. When voters surveyed were shown the official ballot language and statement in WA-8, they supported I-645 by 48% to 43%, with 9% undecided. When biased anti-repeal language was removed and voters were shown the truth, that this is an income tax, support for repeal rose to 67%, with 19% preferring to keep the tax and 14% undecided. In WA-5, voters supported I-645 by 46% to 43%, with 11% undecided. When that language was removed, support for repeal rose to 62%, with 20% preferring to keep the tax and 18% undecided. 

Model Districts Where Elections Are Won or Lost

These Districts are bellwether districts, covering over 7,300 square miles and nearly 800,000 residents across parts of King, Snohomish, Pierce, Kittitas, and Chelan counties, from suburban neighborhoods to Central Washington farmland. CD-5 covers Eastern Washington from Spokane to Walla Walla, with about 800,000 residents across ten counties and parts of two more. With District 8 leaning Democrat (D+3) and District 5 leaning Republican (R+5), these results suggest appeal for repealing the income tax reaches across party lines.

Voters can learn more at voteyes645.com. Ballots are in voters' hands now and are due Nov. 3.

YouTube: @voteyes645

Headquartered in Greenville, South Carolina, Champion Coach is a leading provider of luxury motorcoach transportation services to professional sports teams, collegiate athletic programs, corporate groups, schools and universities, nonprofit organizations, and other customers throughout the United States. This partnership between Champion Coach and HF Companies creates a unique, strategic fit that is well positioned to unlock value for everyone involved. We were proud to advise the Dance family on this important transaction.”

The Company serves a diverse customer base that includes professional sports teams, collegiate athletic programs, corporate groups, schools and universities, nonprofit organizations, and other organizations requiring premium group transportation services. data.title: Novartis U.S. Shares Fall After MS Pill Trial Data Disappoint
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud 




  Novartis's U.S. shares fell after the Swiss drugmaker reported results of two late-stage studies of its multiple sclerosis pill that showed a reduction in flare-ups below that achieved by a rival drug from Roche Holding. 



  American depositary receipts in Novartis fell as much as 4.5% in U.S. midday trading Friday before recovering somewhat, reducing their year-to-date gains. 



  Novartis said its drug, known as remibrutinib and marketed as Rhapsido for skin condition chronic spontaneous urticaria, met the primary goals of the studies by reducing relapse rates relative to Sanofi's rival treatment Aubagio in patients with relapsing MS, the most common form of the disease. The results were presented at scientific congress MSToronto2026 in Toronto and published in medical journal the Lancet. 



  The studies showed the drug achieved reductions in the annualized relapse rate of 35.2% and 31.2% compared to Aubagio, the company said. This translated into one relapse every 13 years, it added. 



  No liver safety signal was observed, Novartis said. 



  Novartis, which was recently hit by trial failures of cholesterol and neuromuscular drugs, already reported initial findings from the studies last month, but analysts said a look at the full data was required to assess how its drug performed against the competitor product from Roche. 



  Roche, Novartis's Swiss cross-town rival, previously said its own multiple sclerosis pill, fenebrutinib, lowered the annualized relapse rate by 51.1% and 58.5% in two late-stage studies, but its drug showed signs of potential liver injury. 



  Analysts at UBS had said before Novartis released the full study data that the company would likely need to deliver efficacy data at least on par with Roche's fenebrutinib with a clean safety profile to trigger a positive market reaction. 



  Novartis said there were no cases that would raise concerns about drug-induced liver injury in its trials. Roche reported a case of potential liver damage. 



  By combining high efficacy with a favorable safety profile, the medicine has the potential to support long-term disease management, Novartis Chief Medical Officer Shreeram Aradhye said. 





  Write to Adria Calatayud at adria.calatayud@wsj.com 





  (END) Dow Jones Newswires

Deadline Alert: Bank Of America Corporation Investors Have Until December 15, 2026 to Seek Lead Plaintiff Role in Securities Fraud Class Action, Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP Reminds Investors

Class action covers investors who bought Bank Of America Corporation securities between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026; complaint alleges the company failed to disclose material adverse facts

Investors in Bank Of America Corporation ("Bank of America" or the "Company") (NYSE: BAC) have until December 15, 2026 to ask the Court to appoint them lead plaintiff in a securities fraud class action lawsuit filed on behalf of investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Bank Of America Corporation securities between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026, inclusive. Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP ("Glancy") today reminded investors of the upcoming deadline. The Bank Of America Corporation case, New England Teamsters Pension Fund v. Bank of America Corporation et al., was filed on October 16, 2026 and is pending in the U.S. District Court Southern District of New York (Case No. 1:26-cv-09137).

Investors who suffered losses on Bank Of America Corporation investments can contact Glancy about the Bank Of America Corporation class action to learn about potentially pursuing claims under the federal securities laws before the December 15, 2026 deadline.

Deadline and key dates for Bank Of America Corporation investors

  • Lead plaintiff deadline: December 15, 2026
  • Class period: August 1, 2025 to October 13, 2026, inclusive
  • Complaint filed: October 16, 2026
  • Court: U.S. District Court Southern District of New York

What happened?

On October 13, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced a $1.2 billion fine against Bank of America Corporation for violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws. According to the Department of the Treasury, Bank of America Corporation failed to mitigate and report priority national security risks. The Department of the Treasury also found that the Company’s Bank Secrecy Act and anti-money laundering compliance programs were deficient and ineffective.

On this news, Bank of America stock fell $2.57 or, 4.76%, to close at $51.39 on October 14, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

What does the Bank Of America Corporation complaint allege?

The Bank Of America Corporation securities lawsuit alleges that, throughout the class period, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about Bank Of America Corporation's business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, the complaint alleges defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (1) systemic weaknesses in BANA's BSA/AML program caused it to fail to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions and to miss, delay, or file inaccurate or incomplete suspicious activity reports involving billions of dollars in suspicious activity; (2) internal reports had documented BANA's BSA/AML deficiencies for years, yet BANA had not adequately remedied them after the 2024 Consent Order; (3) BANA also had deficiencies in its sanctions compliance program and processed transactions later identified as apparent violations of multiple sanctions programs; (4) fixing these deficiencies required significant additional compliance resources and exposed BANA to substantial penalties and costs; and (5) as a result, defendants' positive statements about Bank Of America Corporation's business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis at all relevant times.

Investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Bank Of America Corporation securities during the class period may move the Court no later than December 15, 2026 to request appointment as lead plaintiff in this putative class action lawsuit.

"The complaint against Bank Of America Corporation alleges, among other things, that the Company failed to disclose that systemic weaknesses in BANA's BSA/AML program caused it to fail to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions and to miss, delay, or file inaccurate or incomplete suspicious activity reports involving billions of dollars in suspicious activity. The December 15, 2026 deadline to request appointment as lead plaintiff is approaching, and investors considering that role should act promptly," said Charles H. Linehan, Partner at Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP.

What's the next step?

Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP is a leading national shareholder rights law firm that can help Bank Of America Corporation investors evaluate potential claims to recover their losses. Investors who wish to serve as lead plaintiff in the Bank Of America Corporation class action must move the Court by December 15, 2026. To learn more, visit the Bank Of America Corporation case page, email shareholders@glancylaw.com, or call 310-201-9150 (toll-free: 888-773-9224).

If you inquire by email, please include your mailing address, telephone number, and number of shares purchased.

To be a member of the Bank Of America Corporation class, you need not take any action at this time. You may retain counsel of your choice or take no action and remain an absent class member. No class has been certified yet in the Bank Of America Corporation case.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is eligible? Investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Bank Of America Corporation securities between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026 and suffered losses may be members of the proposed class in the Bank Of America Corporation shareholder lawsuit.

When is the Bank Of America Corporation lead plaintiff deadline? Motions to serve as lead plaintiff in the Bank Of America Corporation class action must be filed with the U.S. District Court Southern District of New York by December 15, 2026.

What if I miss the Bank Of America Corporation deadline? After December 15, 2026, investors generally can no longer ask to be appointed lead plaintiff, but Bank Of America Corporation investors may still remain class members. Their ability to share in any future recovery does not depend on serving as lead plaintiff.

What is a lead plaintiff? In the Bank Of America Corporation class action, the lead plaintiff is the investor, or group of investors, that the court appoints to represent all class members and oversee the case. Under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act, courts generally presume the movant with the largest financial interest is the most adequate lead plaintiff.

Does it cost anything to contact Glancy or participate in this action? Glancy represents Bank Of America Corporation investors on a contingency fee basis, so investors pay no attorneys' fees out of pocket. Any attorneys' fees and litigation expenses are paid only from a recovery, if one is obtained, and are subject to court approval.

Why work with Glancy on the Bank Of America Corporation lawsuit? Glancy was named one of Law360's Securities Groups of the Year and ranked second in total investor recoveries by ISS Securities Class Action Services in 2025.

Glancy's successes have been widely covered by leading news and industry publications, including The Wall Street Journal, The Financial Times, Bloomberg Businessweek, Reuters, the Associated Press, Barron's, Investor's Business Daily, Forbes, and Money.

The suit was filed on behalf of investors who purchased or otherwise acquired the Company's securities from February 7, 2025 through October 2, 2026, inclusive. The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith today highlighted the deadline in the case, Rubenstsein et al. v. What happened?

On October 2, 2026, Hunterbrook published a report alleging that “[c]ontrary to the plans in its initial SEC filings, Millrose has now bought an estimated $200 million of Lennar homes in about a month and is renting them out at what appears to be a loss.” Further, the report stated that although “[a]ccounting rules say a company cannot book a sale to an entity it controls; a forensic accountant told Hunterbrook the question of Lennar’s control over Millrose seems ‘black and white’ in spirit[.”]

On this news, Millrose stock fell $2.10 per share, or 8.53%, to close at $22.51 on October 5, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

Allegations in the Millrose Properties, Inc. case

The Millrose Properties, Inc. shareholder lawsuit alleges that, throughout the class period, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about Millrose Properties, Inc.'s business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, the complaint alleges defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (1) despite representations to the contrary, Millrose's objectives were not limited to engaging in land purchases, horizontal development, and homesite option purchase arrangements for Lennar and potentially other homebuilders and developers; (2) despite representations to the contrary, Millrose would in fact enter into lease agreements and would have tenants in its properties; (3) Millrose would purchase $200 million worth of properties from Lennar; (4) Millrose would lease the properties purchased from Lennar out at a loss; and (5) as a result, defendants' positive statements about Millrose Properties, Inc.'s business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis at all relevant times.

Millrose Properties, Inc. investors who purchased or otherwise acquired securities during the class period may move the Court by December 8, 2026 to seek appointment as lead plaintiff in this putative class action.

data.title: PureTalk Customers Help Raise More Than $1 Million For Veterans
data.description:
COVINGTON, GA / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / PureTalk, the Veteran-led wireless company known for offering premium wireless service at a fraction of the cost of major carriers, today announced it has raised more than $1 million for America's Warrior Partnership (AWP), a national nonprofit that connects Veterans and their families with supportive community resources and services to help improve and save Veterans' lives. The total combines monthly roundups where customers round their bill up to the nearest dollar, one-time customer donations and company matching campaigns, including a recent PureTalk match of $250,000 during the company's America250 campaign this summer. Every donated dollar goes to AWP and its programs

"Building a community network to recognize and support the unique needs of Veterans and their families is at the heart of the American's Warrior Partnership mission," said Jim Lorraine, president and CEO of America's Warrior Partnership. "PureTalk takes that concept and puts it into action. We are grateful for PureTalk's partnership and their leading a groundswell of meaningful community support among their customers to measurably improve the lives of Veterans and their loved ones."

"My dad gets his care from the VA, so the Deeds Not Words initiative is personal," said William Curry, Chief Strategy Officer at Telrite Holdings. "We have Veterans to thank for ensuring America's way of life. We want to help ensure theirs."

"Veterans need a hand up, not a handout," said Clint Romesha, Medal of Honor recipient and AWP board member Emeritus. "Since 2023, PureTalk and America's Warrior Partnership have been working to give Veterans the support they need; we've raised over $1 million in that effort," he continued. "That's the definition of Deeds Not Words, right there."

Marine Corps Veteran David Bennett received mortgage assistance that kept his family in their home after his wife unexpectedly lost her job.

"Me and my family fell on some hard times, and we didn't know if we'd be able to keep our home," Bennett said.

Army Reserve Veteran Dale Dyer was recovering from a serious injury that kept him out of work when the family's vehicle broke down. AWP and PureTalk covered the repair so he could return to work.

The support continues. New PureTalk customers can start a monthly round-up or make a one-time donation when they sign up for PureTalk wireless service, or existing customers can donate through their online account. Details are available at PureTalk.com/roundup.

About PureTalk

PureTalk, a subsidiary of Telrite Holdings, Inc., is a Veteran-led wireless provider that offers superior wireless plans backed by a dependable nationwide 5G network at a fraction of the cost of major carriers. With 100% U.S.-based operations, including customer service, PureTalk built its reputation on honesty, integrity, and delivering real value to its customers. PureTalk is committed to supporting hardworking Americans and the military members who serve our country. Together with its customers, PureTalk has contributed more than $1 million to America's Warrior Partnership and helped eliminate $10 million in veteran debt. It supports K9s For Warriors, mikeroweWORKS Foundation, and other organizations that help Veterans and their families. For more information, visit PureTalk.com.

About America's Warrior Partnership

America's Warrior Partnership is a national 501(c)(3) nonprofit that connects Veterans, their families and caregivers with resources, services and partnerships in their own communities. AWP works through its community integration model, the AWP Network and research initiatives that include Operation Deep Dive, a multi-year study of Veteran suicide and other non-natural deaths. Learn more at americaswarriorpartnership.org.

data.title: bp and the State of Louisiana agree to resolve long-standing matters and open a new chapter
data.description:
bp and the State of Louisiana agree to resolve long-standing matters and open a new chapter

bp and the State of Louisiana agree to resolve long-standing matters and open a new chapter

PR Newswire

HOUSTON, Oct. 23, 2026

Agreement gives Louisiana its remaining Deepwater Horizon economic damages payments in a single early payment and resolves the remaining coastal zone lawsuits involving bp

HOUSTON, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- bp and the State of Louisiana ('Louisiana') today announced an agreement to resolve two long-standing legacy matters, delivering Deepwater Horizon funds to the state now and resetting the relationship between bp and Louisiana so both can focus on the future.

Under the agreement, signed by Governor Jeff Landry, Attorney General Liz Murrill and bp chief executive officer Meg O'Neill:

  • bp will bring forward its remaining payments to Louisiana under the 2015 Deepwater Horizon Economic Damages Settlement into a single early payment of approximately $350 million – giving the state certainty and access to the funds now, rather than over the next seven years.
  • The remaining coastal zone lawsuits brought by Louisiana parishes to which bp is a party will be resolved, bringing long-running litigation to a close.

Meg O'Neill, bp chief executive officer, said: "We will never forget the 11 men who lost their lives, or the impact on their families, communities and the environment across the Gulf Coast. Deepwater Horizon was a tragedy that forever changed bp, and the lessons we learned continue to guide how we operate today.

This agreement with Louisiana accelerates the delivery of our commitments and provides the state with access to these funds now. I would like to thank Governor Jeff Landry and Attorney General Liz Murrill for their leadership in reaching this agreement."

Governor Jeff Landry said: "I want to thank bp for coming to the table. Unresolved issues, like these, hold Louisiana back. As Governor I have worked to responsibly and ethically, clean up the litigation environment that has impacted one of our largest employers—the oil and gas industry. This is just another step in fulfilling my promise.

We have tackled legacy lawsuits, which many said was impossible. We have now disposed of claims and settled with all but one of the major defendants in these coastal cases. This sends a signal to job creators all over America that Louisiana welcomes jobs and economic growth while responsibly dealing with the issues of the past.

We appreciate bp's commitment and investment in Louisiana and look forward to a great partnership in producing the energy needed to fuel opportunity in Louisiana."

Attorney General Liz Murrill said: "Louisiana has been a leader in defending, building, and protecting energy security nationally and internationally. I'm grateful to join Governor Landry and bp America as we build a stable energy supply. Resolving issues of the past paves our way to a brighter future working relationship."

Orlando Alvarez, chairman and president, bp America, said: "Louisiana is home to more than 800 bp employees, and our business here – from the Haynesville to the Gulf of America – is central to bp's future in the US. Resolving these matters strengthens the foundation for our work in the state, and we're proud to keep building that future with Louisiana."

bp is a significant energy investor in the State of Louisiana. In 2025, the company spent $590 million with Louisiana vendors and paid more than $280 million in royalties and property and franchise taxes in the state. bp is one of the largest producers, leaseholders and investors in the Gulf of America, and through bpx energy holds a strong position in the Haynesville.

Notes to editors

• In 2015, bp reached agreements to settle federal, state and local government claims arising from the 2010 Deepwater Horizon accident for up to $18.7 billion, with payments spread over 18 years. The settlement was approved by a federal court in April 2016.

• Under the settlement, $4.9 billion is payable over 18 years to settle economic and other claims made by the five Gulf Coast states.

• Under the existing schedule, bp's remaining payments of $373 million to Louisiana under the Economic Damages Settlement are due in equal payments with no interest over the next seven years. The agreement replaces these with a single payment of approximately $350 million.

• The Louisiana agreement represents more than 20% of bp's outstanding payments to the five Gulf states under the Economic Damages Settlement.

• For more information on bp's Gulf of America annual payment schedule: Gulf of America oil spill Government settlements – expected pre-tax cash flow schedule

data.title: 'Some people did everything right': I lost my home in the Great Recession. I rent in my 50s. Why is that judged as failure?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'I earn $110,000 a year'

"Saving for a down payment is not easy in a major metropolitan area when a house costs three to four times your annual income." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I read the letter about mortgage applications and your response (As a mortgage loan officer, I rejected wealthy couples. Here's what can get your application declined.), and I agree with much of what this reader says. Living within your means, avoiding (unnecessary) debt and saving are good advice. There's a lot to be said for the discipline of "Joe Six-Pack," as the mortgage loan officer described him, who earns less but saves and eventually buys a home.

But there's another side of this that often gets overlooked - which, in fairness, you did address somewhat in your answer. I'm in my 50s, and the Great Recession hit at the worst time in my life. I wasn't a fool, but I did try to build a life for myself by buying a house. Still, the housing crash had consequences that lasted far longer than the recession itself. I lost my job and eventually my home. I earn $110,000 a year and it's still hard.

For people my age, getting knocked off the property ladder can be very hard to recover from. Those who already owned a home and held on to it through the downturn benefited enormously from the rise in property values that followed. Those who lost a home, sold at the wrong time or couldn't buy during those years missed out on that appreciation entirely. It was a matter of timing for many people, not reckless abandon as the mortgage loan officer would like us to believe.

Some people did everything right and were caught on the wrong side of an economic shock. Let me also tell you that saving for a down payment is not easy in a major metropolitan area when a house costs three to four times your annual income. So my message to your letter writer is to be careful about turning a lesson in spending too much into a judgment of people who haven't hit the same milestones. I am happy for friends and family who have homes, but it still stings.

Why judge other people for not getting on the property ladder?

Renter in His 50s

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: I'm 77, pay rent and live off Social Security, but I help homeless people. Why are so many people going hungry?

Homeownership in the U.S. has averaged 61% in Gallup polls since 2012, down from 70% between 2001 and 2011.

Dear Renter,

We are all on our own paths, and I'd bet that people who judge others for having less are insecure around those who have more.

You did not come out of the 2008-09 recession unscathed, and I can see why it rankles when somebody in a position of authority, even power, talks critically about would-be homebuyers putting too much money on credit cards or not saving enough of their salary, even though they earn a six-figure income. You have a right to feel the way you do, and you furthermore have a right to express it. I'm glad you chose to do that here.

For the record, the mortgage loan officer in question struck me as alarmist and at times judgmental. "People in the U.S. need to wake up and not be compulsive," she wrote. "Quit buying things you really don't need. It's that way with the federal government as well, and based on that, we'd better get real quick or we're going to have a financial crisis that makes the Great Recession of 2008 look like a picnic."

It's painful to have had a home once upon a time only to lose it, and to realize how much you lost. It was, sad to say, not an uncommon story during the last recession, when the unemployment rate rose to 10% and the number of foreclosure filings hit 2.8 million in 2009. I believe it helps enormously to know that this was a shared, collective trauma, and that many millions of people around the world also went through what you experienced.

Many millions of people around the world went through what you experienced.

High interest rates - the 30-year mortgage rate hit 7.3% in early October, nearly three times its level five years ago - and high house prices mean that buying a home remains out of reach for people who no longer have home equity to leverage, as well as for many first-time buyers. There's also a dearth of inventory in many markets, which has led to a generation of renters in their 30s, 40s, 50s and beyond. It can be a bitter pill to swallow.

At $110,000 a year, or $9,200 a month before taxes, lenders prefer housing costs at or below 30% of gross income. If you took a mortgage rate of 7.3%, even with money set aside for property taxes and insurance, you could afford a $300,000 property. That amount would be further reduced by student debt, a car payment and/or credit-card debt. And that's before you pull the money together for a down payment.

You would need to drum up $90,000 for a 20% down payment. That makes your task even more challenging after a job loss or foreclosure. Location matters too, as you say you live in a major metropolitan area. In the Midwest and South, $110,000 could buy a decent home, but in the New York, Boston, Los Angeles or Seattle areas, median prices can top $800,000, depending on the neighborhood.

Related: 'I don't want to die on the sales floor': I'm 67 and earn $19.50 an hour at a big-box store. When can I finally retire?

Homeownership rates have fallen

A recent Gallup poll shed light on what you are experiencing, and the results did not bode well for a generation of renters who would like to get their foot on the property ladder. The share of U.S. non-homeowners who expect to buy a home within five years has dropped to 25%, the lowest level Gallup has recorded since it began asking the question more than a decade ago. The poll found that 61% of Americans say they own their primary residence, while 34% rent.

Homeownership in the U.S. has averaged 61% in Gallup polls since 2012. Some 28% of non-homeowners told Gallup that they expect to buy a home within 10 years and just 25% said they expect to do so within five years, while 45% do not think they will do so at all in the foreseeable future. More worryingly, all of those figures have dropped over the past 10 years.

My colleagues Jillian Berman and Venessa Wong recently wrote about young Americans who feel shut out of the housing market - seemingly forever, in some cases. As they pointed out, the median age of renters in America now hovers around 42, up from 38 in 2006, and nearly one-third of renters have a college degree or higher, compared with 22% in 2010, according to Census Bureau data. Meanwhile, the national average rent is now $1,665 per month.

Renters are getting older, even if younger adults make up the largest share.

There has been some good news for renters. A 2026 report on rental housing from Harvard's Joint Center for Housing Studies said that after record-high increases during the pandemic, national rent growth has stayed near zero since mid-2023. Most markets experienced either small declines or small increases. In 74 of the largest 150 markets, asking rents fell, while 70 recorded modest growth of less than 4%. Rents rose by 4% or more in only six markets.

Perhaps the most significant takeaway is that renters are getting older, even if younger adults still make up the largest share of the renting population. Although there were roughly 6.1 million renters in your age group (50-59) in 2024, that number is down from 6.7 million in 2014. But there were more renters ages 60 to 69 (5.4 million versus 4.4 million in 2014) and 70 to 79 (3.4 million versus 2.3 million). That is a mixed picture at best.

Some 13% of renters are in their 50s, based on the most recent data from the U.S. Census Bureau. Adding up all those people from the JCHS report, 10.9 million people ages 60 and over are renters. That affects their financial security now and when they retire. Housing remains the biggest monthly expense for most people, and having to pay rent in your 60s does not make retirement any easier. Keep on saving and planning.

Take a bow. You are a survivor and, given the kind of upheaval you have endured, you are living a different kind of American dream.

Related: I'm 71 and still working. I earn $108,000 a year. Am I doing the right thing?

CCAGW Endorses Candidates

Today, the Council for Citizens Against Government Waste (CCAGW) announced its endorsement of 12 candidates for the U.S. Senate, 123 candidates for the U.S. House of Representatives, and six candidates for governor. The candidates have been endorsed based on their lifetime rating in CCAGW’s 2025 Congressional Ratings.

“During their tenures in the Senate and House, these members of Congress have been strong and reliable votes to curb government waste and reform Washington,” said CCAGW President Tom Schatz. “On top of their impressive voting records, they fought for increased accountability and transparency while opposing efforts to increase federal spending and adopt burdensome new regulations. I urge voters to elect and re-elect them to the U.S. Senate, the U.S. House of Representatives, and state governorships.”

data.title: The Week in Oil: Fears of U.S.-Iran Escalation Push Brent to $117
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni 




  Here is a look at what happened in oil markets in the week of Oct. 19-23 and what the focus will be in the days to come. 





  OVERVIEW: Oil prices are on track for another weekly gain on fears of renewed escalation between the U.S. and Iran after the midterm elections. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was around $117 a barrel in midmorning U.S. trade, while West Texas Intermediate was just below $103 a barrel. 





  MACRO: Rising energy costs are fueling concerns over inflation and interest-rate hikes. According to the FedWatch tool, traders broadly expect the U.S. central bank to leave interest rates unchanged next week, but they see a nearly 80% probability of a hike in December. 



  Meanwhile, consumer sentiment in the U.S. ticked lower in October, hovering near record-low levels, according to the University of Michigan's survey. Inflation expectations instead moved slightly higher. 





  GEOPOLITICAL RISKS: Fears that the U.S. could attack Iran after the midterm elections in early November are driving oil's rise this week. The U.S. has a third aircraft carrier strike group and an additional Marine expeditionary unit en route to the Middle East, while the military has moved some troops off bases in the region. 



  The buildup comes at a politically sensitive moment, with Israel's general election scheduled for Oct. 27 and the U.S. midterms a week later. 



  Tehran warned that a renewed U.S. and Israeli air campaign would prompt retaliation extending well beyond military targets. Iran threatened strikes on American bases and warships, as well as airports, pipelines and other civilian infrastructure in neighboring Persian Gulf countries. 



  At the same time, persistent attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and deadly strikes by Yemen's Houthi militants on Saudi Arabia are keeping the geopolitical risk premium high. The market's focus is less on how much oil is available today than on whether Middle East exports can be sustained if fighting intensifies again. 





  SUPPLY AND DEMAND: Kpler data show that oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain 26% below prewar levels, with the seven-day average at 12.65 million barrels a day, compared with a baseline of 17.15 million. Continued attacks on shipping are sustaining a risk premium in both freight rates and crude prices. Yet total Middle Eastern oil supplies reaching global markets, excluding Iran, remain above prewar levels. 



  Meanwhile, shipment of Russian diesel could be headed for the U.S., according to vessel-tracking data, potentially signaling a return of direct fuel deliveries as U.S. President Trump seeks to expand Russian supplies to international markets. 





  WHAT'S AHEAD: Markets will turn to the Federal Reserve's policy meeting on Oct. 27-28 and the release of the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the personal consumption expenditures price index, on Oct. 29 for clues on the outlook for interest rates. On the energy front, next week's focus will be on any signs of a potential escalation between the U.S. and Iran, fresh data on crude and refined-product inventories, and developments in Russian diesel shipments. 





  Write to Giulia Petroni at giulia.petroni@wsj.com
